brief:
Lewis Hamilton used Rwanda's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix as a platform to demand freedom for Palestinians and the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to Al Jazeera English. The Mercedes driver renewed his long-standing advocacy for Palestinian rights while extending his appeal to include the eastern African nation amid international scrutiny over Rwanda's human rights record.

Hamilton's dual call for liberation came as the country prepared to host its first-ever Grand Prix, an event that has drawn criticism from rights groups concerned about the government's record. The driver has previously used major sporting platforms to highlight political causes and humanitarian concerns.
dek: Rwanda's controversial Formula One GP leads Lewis Hamilton to call for freedom for DR Congo, while renewing Palestine plea.
title: Hamilton calls for Palestinian and Congolese freedom as Rwanda hosts F1 race
